observation_summary: The CSVPrinter outputs escaped versions of the nullString (e.g., '\\N') instead of the literal nullString (e.g., '\N') when writing null values.
reasoning_summary: The issue arises because the CSVPrinter incorrectly applies escaping rules to the configured 'nullString' value. When the printer encounters a null value, it replaces it with the configured nullString (e.g., '\N'), but then proceeds to pass this string through the same escaping logic used for regular data fields. This causes the null representation to be double-escaped or incorrectly modified (e.g., '\N' becoming '\\N'), which violates the expected format for MySQL compatibility. The tests fail because the output contains these extra escape characters instead of the literal null representation.
